en: cook rice in caramelised onion stock

does: Simmers deeply browned onions in water with cumin to make a dark, sweet broth, then cooks washed long-grain rice in the strained broth under a lid until it is taken up, so that the grains come out brown and full of the taste of the onions.
how: Fry the onions dark first and keep the oil they leave.
Simmer most of the onions in water with cumin and salt, then strain or blend the broth.
Coat the washed rice in a spoonful of the onion oil.
Pour in the measured hot broth, bring it to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat until the broth is taken up.
Leave it covered off the heat, then fluff it with a fork.

cues.text: The broth is a deep amber brown, and the cooked rice is evenly brown.
The rice tastes sweet and deep of browned onion, not burnt.

mistakes.mistake: Using onions that were only golden, so that the broth and the rice stay pale and flat.
mistakes.fix: Take the onions to a deep brown.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the lid while the rice cooks, so that the steam escapes and the grains stay hard.
mistakes.fix: Keep the lid on until the end.

comes_after.why: The broth is made from onions fried dark.

variant_of.differs: The rice is cooked in a broth made from deeply fried onions, which turns it brown and sweet, rather than with sweated onion in stock.
